tagline.text: The port town at the northern tip of mainland Cebu, where boats leave for Malapascua

location.label: Location
location.text: Northern tip of mainland Cebu Province, around Maya Port

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–3,500 (per person, one night at Maya Port from Cebu City)

children.text: Daanbantayan is the municipality at the northern tip of mainland Cebu, home to Maya Port, from which boats leave for Malapascua Island. It is also known for the Santa Rosa de Lima church in town and the Haladaya Festival in August.

Daanbantayan is a municipality at the very northern tip of mainland Cebu, bordered by the Visayan Sea to the north, Bantayan Island across the water to the west, the Camotes Sea to the east and Medellin to the south. It is about 136 km from Cebu City, covers about 92 km², and had about 95,000 residents in 2024 in 20 barangays, making it a first-class municipality. The name combines "daan" (old) and "bantayan" (lookout), and is said to come from a watch post used to spot Moro raiders in the past.

For travelers, this town is above all a gateway. Boats to Malapascua Island leave from Barangay Maya at the northern end, and Madridejos on Bantayan Island faces it across the water to the west. So most travelers do not stay long here; they sleep near Maya Port and take the next boat. But if you have time, there is surprisingly much to see: the beaches of Maya, the church in town and the festival in August.

In town stands the Santa Rosa de Lima church (the Archdiocesan Shrine of Santa Rosa de Lima), which opened in 1858 and was completed in 1886. An old coral-stone church, it lost part of its front in the magnitude 6.9 northern Cebu earthquake of September 30, 2025. Reports say that as of February 2026 restoration was about half done and some of the facade decoration had been recovered, so check whether it is open before you go. The plaza, the San Pedro River and Tapilon Point are other historical spots in town. The municipal hall was built in 1916, and reports say Calle Santa Rosa in front of the church, now cleared of debris, will reopen once Phase 1 of the restoration is finished.

Daanbantayan was badly hit both by Typhoon Yolanda in 2013 and by the 2025 earthquake. It was in an Intensity VII zone in the quake, and reports said the damage here was greater than in neighboring municipalities. Recovery is still under way, so visitors should take care not to disturb residents' daily lives.

Public bangkas run from Maya Port to Malapascua Island, and the crossing takes about 30–45 minutes. There are two harbors, Old Maya Port and New Maya Port, and notes say Ceres buses go to the new port and other buses to the old one. For the island side, see the
Malapascua Island
entry.

Maya is known for a beach with fine sand, calm water, floating cottages and viewing decks. There are seafood restaurants, cafés and bars, and a new food hub, Tambayan sa Maya, is compared to Sugbo Mercado in Cebu City. Maya is the northernmost barangay of Daanbantayan, where a white-sand beach and seafood restaurants are close at hand.

The coral-stone church in the town center is one of Cebu's historic churches. The 2025 earthquake collapsed part of its facade decoration, and according to a February 2026 report, workers have cleared about half of the debris and are documenting and retrieving 30 19th-century components, including decoration carved with an 1886 inscription. It is protected under the National Cultural Heritage Act (RA 10066), so do not take fragments as souvenirs.

Held from August 21 to 30, this is the town's biggest festival, honoring its legendary founder, Datu Daya. It ends with street dancing on the last day. The town is busy during the festival, so check lodging and transport ahead.

A working lighthouse more than 100 years old stands on a hilltop and is said to have a good sea view. Check its exact location and whether it is open on site. The path and hill below the lighthouse may be steep, so wear comfortable shoes.

Administratively, Daanbantayan also includes Gato Island (a rocky islet about 83 m high) and Monad Shoal (a seamount about 20 m deep, known for thresher sharks), around Malapascua Island. Dive trips are usually booked at dive shops on the Malapascua side.

The Daanbantayan pier is described as a gateway to the beaches and historic sites of Bantayan Island, and you can stroll along the waterfront nearby. Passenger routes and timetables change often, so check locally.
There is a boat route from Malapascua to Bantayan, but it is irregular. If you want to see both, it is safer to split the overland trip between Hagnaya and Maya over two days.

Daanbantayan is best in the dry season,
December–May
. The sea is calm, so boats to Malapascua run reliably and skies are clear. During the Haladaya Festival,
August 21–30
, the town is busy, so catch it if your dates match. Midday temperatures are usually around
, and the sun is strong, so bring a hat and sunscreen.
In the rainy season,
June–November

September–November

Around Maya Port there are small guesthouses and beach resorts, widely used by travelers heading to Malapascua Island for a night. Prices and room numbers vary greatly by season, so book ahead. Lodging information differs by source, so it is better to confirm an exact list on site.

Maya has restaurants, bars and cafés, and a new food hub, Tambayan sa Maya, is said to be popular. Beach restaurants serve fresh seafood, and it is convenient to prepare water, snacks and cash before crossing to Malapascua. ATMs on the island are few.
If you take a morning boat, buy water, snacks and breakfast the evening before. It is safer to withdraw enough cash before you cross to the island.
Plan to reach Maya Port by 3 PM. There is no confirmed information on the last boat time.
There are two ports (Old Maya Port and New Maya Port). When boarding a bus, ask the conductor which one it stops at.
A bangka leaves only when it is full. To go faster, travel together as a larger group or consider chartering.
Keep your luggage in a waterproof bag or plastic. Water can splash when the boat rocks.
Taking an early-morning bus gives you room to catch a morning boat at Maya Port. Check the first bus time at the North Terminal counter.
This area was hit by the 2025 earthquake. Take photos and visit with respect for residents' lives.

Daanbantayan is among the areas most damaged by the September 30, 2025 northern Cebu earthquake. The church and some coastal facilities are under repair, so check locally on openings and access restrictions.
Boat service is suspended depending on weather. Check PAGASA warnings and municipal announcements, and leave slack in your schedule.
Port and environmental fees differ by source. Get a receipt and check the amount.
Do not take fragments from the church restoration site as souvenirs. They are covered by the national heritage protection law.
After 5 PM, the public bangkas stop and you may need a chartered boat. Beware of inflated prices.
Bus timetables change often. Check departure times at the North Terminal counter.
Motorcycles may not be carried on passenger ferries or bangkas. It is better to leave your motorcycle behind when going to Malapascua.
